title: On the use of case estimate and transactional payment data in neural networks for individual loss reserving
abstract: arXiv:2601.05274v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The use of neural networks trained on individual claims data has become increasingly popular in the actuarial reserving literature. We consider how to best input historical payment data in neural network models. Additionally, case estimates are also available in the format of a time series, and we extend our analysis to assessing their predictive power. In this paper, we compare a feed-forward neural network trained on summarised transactions to a recurrent neural network equipped to analyse a claim's entire payment history and/or case estimate development history. We draw conclusions from training and comparing the performance of the models on multiple, comparable highly complex datasets simulated from SPLICE (Avanzi, Taylor and Wang, 2023). translated_title: 论在个体损失准备金评估的神经网络中使用个案估计与交易赔付数据
translated_abstract: 在精算准备金文献中，使用基于个体索赔数据训练的神经网络已日益流行。我们研究了如何在神经网络模型中最优地输入历史赔付数据。此外，个案估计也以时间序列的形式存在，我们进一步扩展了分析以评估其预测能力。在本文中，我们将基于汇总交易数据训练的前馈神经网络与能够分析索赔完整赔付历史和/或个案估计发展历史的循环神经网络进行了比较。我们通过在由SPLICE（Avanzi、Taylor和Wang，2023）模拟出的多个可比较的高度复杂数据集上训练并比较各模型的性能，从而得出结论。在协变量数据有限的环境中，我们发现有证据表明个案估计能够显著改善预测效果，但为神经网络配备记忆机制只会带来……（原文摘要至此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文比较了前馈神经网络（使用汇总交易数据）与循环神经网络（使用完整赔付历史及个案估计发展历史）在个体损失准备金评估中的表现，发现在协变量数据有限的情况下，个案估计能显著提升预测效果，而赋予神经网络记忆机制的额外收益则相对有限。
en_tdlr: This paper compares a feed-forward neural network trained on summarised transactions with a recurrent neural network analysing a claim's full payment and case estimate development histories for individual loss reserving, finding that case estimates substantially improve predictions when covariate data is limited, while equipping the network with memory yields only limited additional gains.
